newsitem.title: USA: Virginia Power says 377,000 without power.
newsitem.headline: Virginia Power says 377,000 without power.

text.p: Virginia Power, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources Inc, said Friday about 377,000 of its customers were without power as Hurricane Fran rolled into its Virginia and North Carolina service territory.
"As of 0810 (EDT), about 377,000 customers were without power due to high winds. This may be the largest outage in the company's history," the company said in a statement.
The company said in central Virginia, the hardest hit area, about 143,000 customers were without electricity, including 92,000 in the Richmond area, where the company has its headquarters.
"Several transmission lines in Virginia and North Carolina have also failed due to high winds," the company said.

Hurricane Fran was downgraded to a tropical storm early Friday as it moved north-northwest through Virginia after roaring ashore last night near Cape Fear, on North Carolina's southernmost coast, with winds of about 120 mph.
It is still dumping heavy rains on the region.
Virginia Power said its emergency crews would be deployed as soon as it was safe, but that their efforts still were being hampered by strong winds.
